capitals.name: Gythium (Gytheio)
capitals.note: Gythium is called the most important city (League page, paraphrased); the page does not call it a capital and the league had no single seat on the pages opened. Coordinates are Gytheio's. Not a seat 146 BC to 22 BC, when the cities belonged to the Lacedaemonian League.

correction.text: the coastal Laconian cities inhabited by perioikoi, 'independent under Achean protection', Gythium the most important

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no League of Free Laconians; checked with the gazetteer on 2026-10-19, a 30 km disc round Gytheio falls in Greek City-States (4 cells) in 190 and 150, the Roman Republic in 100 and 50 and the Roman Empire from year 0 to 250. The pages name no city except Gythium and Las (the League page) and give no area; the shape is the two 15 km discs round Gytheio and Monemvasia that peloponnesian-league's 195 loss uses, so the two dossiers mirror. Las, captured by the Spartans in 192 and retaliated against by the Achaeans, is inside the Gytheio disc.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the same coastal discs. The page gives no list of the 24 cities and no area; 146-22 BC has no shape because the cities belonged to the Lacedaemonian League.

region.text: the coastal Laconian cities, Gythium first

ledger.note: 195: the coastal Laconian cities become independent under Achaean protection. Infobox: 'Laconian coastal cities become independent under Achean protection as League of Free Laconians'; Flamininus 'separated all coastal cities of Laconia from Spartan rule'. The League page has the Free Laconians 'first mentioned in 195 BC'.
195: Achaean protection. The cities are placed 'under Achean protection' and the fleet of Sparta put 'under custody of these coastal cities'.

region.text: Gythium, besieged by Nabis, and neighbouring Las

ledger.note: 192: Nabis besieges Gythium. 'By 192, Nabis who had built a new fleet and strengthened his army, besieged Gythium' (the League page: 'in 192 BC, Gythium was recaptured by Nabis of Sparta'; Spartan forces then took Las). The Achaeans under Philopoemen were beaten outside Gythium and ravaged Laconia for thirty days.

192 (bridge): the siege ends. No page opened says how Nabis's hold on Gythium ended; the peloponnesian-league dossier dates Nabis's overthrow and Sparta's forced entry into the Achaean League to 192 (Philopoemen).
146: the Achaean League dissolves. 'Following the dissolution of the Achaean League in 146 BC' the Free Laconians' protector is gone.

146: the cities join the Lacedaemonian League. after the dissolution of the Achaean League the Free Laconians joined the Lacedaemonian League, a koinon of Spartan colonies under Roman rule (the page, paraphrased); no separate dossier exists for that koinon.
21 BC: Augustus re-establishes the League of Free Laconians. 'until Emperor Augustus re-established the League of Free Laconians in 21 BC'; at its height it included 24 cities (paraphrased).
297: the koinon ends. It 'continued until 297 AD when the Emperor Diocletian reformed the provincial administration'.

wars.name: War against Nabis

zones.text: the Laconian coast, taken from Sparta in 195

wars.outcome: Flamininus besieged Sparta and Nabis surrendered Argos and the coastal cities of Laconia and his fleet; the cities became the League of Free Laconians under Achaean protection.
wars.note: The page gives 195 for the settlement; the war's own span is not stated on the page.

wars.name: Nabis's war on Gythium
wars.outcome: Nabis besieged and retook Gythium and took Las; the Achaean fleet was beaten by Sparta's new fleet and Philopoemen could not defeat the Spartans outside Gythium; the Achaeans then ravaged Laconia for thirty days.
wars.note: The outcome of the siege is not on either page (see the 192 contest_end).

certainty.note: The pages name Gythium and Las only; the shape is two discs and the real extent of the coastal cities and their territory is not given.

notes: Two pages. The page treats the League as formally established by Augustus in 21 BC, giving structure to cities associated for nearly two centuries (paraphrased), and as first mentioned in 195; this dossier starts at 195 because that is when the cities leave Sparta (the War against Nabis infobox), and counts 146-22 as a break in which the cities sit in the Lacedaemonian League (no dossier exists for it; the counterpart string stands for it). Only Gythium and Las are named in the pages; the 24 cities (Pausanias's list is not on the page) are not drawn individually, and the coastal discs are shared with peloponnesian-league for mirroring. The Roman-imperial life, 21 BC to 297 AD, is outside this batch's era and is kept to the page's dates only. The gazetteer resolves Monemvasia but not Gytheio (the same name peloponnesian-league uses; a place name for the gazetteer agent, 36.76 N 22.57 E). Not on any page opened: the end of Nabis's hold on Gythium (192 is a bridge), the territories of Boiai, Asopos and the other cities, Free Laconian membership under the Achaean League after 192 (the achaean-league dossier does not draw them), the 'Lacedaemonian League' as a state.
